The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of iron, even at low levels, is essential for the growth of L. ivanovi, while the presence of low levels of iron and acid stress is not sufficient to induce a significant ATR in this species.

, in contrast to L. mono­cytogenes, L. ivano­vii is not able to mount a robust ATR and is more sensitive to low iron availability, suggesting that these two stresses may be responsible for the rarity of human infection caused by this species.
